svg.aria-label: Diagram: Azure deployment scopes, showing the four targetScope values and which scopes each deployment can reach through modules, what each scope can host, the rule that every resource keyword declaration must deploy at the deployment's own scope while modules trigger nested deployments that can cross scopes, the requirement for a deployment location at every scope above resource group, and the immutable pairing of deployment name and location
svg.title: Azure deployment scopes: the template's scope is not where the resources land, and a module is the only way across
svg.text: The deployment’s scope and the resources’ scope are two different things.
Every resource declaration lands at the deployment’s own scope. A module starts a nested deployment, and that is the only way across.
Four target scopes, and what each one can host directly
targetScope
What lives there
Needs a location
'tenant'
management groups, subscription aliases, role assignments, billing
yes
custom policy definitions cannot be deployed here
'managementGroup'
policy definitions and assignments, role definitions, nested deployments
yes
'subscription'
resource groups, policy, role assignments, locks, budgets, tags,
diagnostic settings, security settings
yes
'resourceGroup'
everything else — the resources that do the work
no, the group’s own location is used
The deployment location is where deployment data is stored. It is separate from the location of the resources being deployed.
Crossing a scope: the module is the mechanism, the scope function names the target
The rule
Every resource declared with the resource keyword must
deploy at the same scope as the deployment.
Two exemptions:
an existing resource may be referenced at any scope, and
a module deploys wherever its scope property points.
The four scope functions
tenant()
managementGroup(name)
subscription(subscriptionId)
resourceGroup(subscriptionId, name)
A module is a nested deployment, so it gets its own name.
Permission does not cross with the module. The principal deploying the parent must be able to deploy at every scope the modules reach.
The name and location of a deployment are welded together, for ever
For each deployment name, the location is immutable. A deployment named deployment1 created in centralus cannot later be
created as deployment1 in westus. The error is InvalidDeploymentLocation.
And the default deployment name is the template file name — so every pipeline in the estate deploys something called main.
Name deployments explicitly, and put the region in the name if the same template is deployed to more than one.
Tenant scope is not a place you deploy by accident
The Global Administrator does not automatically have permission to assign roles. Enabling tenant deployments takes two deliberate
steps: elevate access, then assign Owner or Contributor at the root scope “/” to the principal that will deploy.
Creating a management group needs Contributor at the tenant; creating a role assignment needs Owner.
Sources: Bicep deploy to subscription, deploy to tenant, deploy to management group, and Understand scope, on Microsoft Learn.
